figs.name: 2-wire-and-4-wire-transmitter-wiring-diagram
figs.alt: 2 wire and 4 wire transmitter wiring diagram with DC supply and PLC analog input
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog comparing a loop powered 2 wire transmitter in series with a DC supply and PLC input against a 4 wire transmitter with separate power and signal pairs.
figs.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 520" width="100%" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif">
<title>2 wire and 4 wire transmitter wiring diagram with power supply and PLC analog input</title>
<rect width="800" height="520" fill="#ffffff"/>
<defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0 0L10 5L0 10z" fill="#1a2b4a"/></marker></defs>
<text x="400.0" y="34" font-size="24" fill="#1e3a8a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">2 Wire vs 4 Wire Transmitter Wiring</text>
<rect x="15" y="60" width="380" height="370" rx="14" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="405" y="60" width="380" height="370" rx="14" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="205" y="90" font-size="20" fill="#1e3a8a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">2 wire: loop powered</text>
<text x="595" y="90" font-size="20" fill="#1e3a8a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">4 wire: separate power</text>
<rect x="35" y="120" width="130" height="70" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="100.0" y="149.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">DC supply</text>
<text x="100.0" y="172.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">loop power</text>
<rect x="235" y="120" width="140" height="70" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="305.0" y="149.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Transmitter</text>
<text x="305.0" y="172.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">field device</text>
<rect x="130" y="320" width="160" height="70" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="210.0" y="349.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">PLC analog</text>
<text x="210.0" y="372.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">input</text>
<line x1="165" y1="140" x2="233" y2="140" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="199" y="128" font-size="20" fill="#dc2626" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">+</text>
<polyline points="305,190 305,355 292,355" fill="none" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<polyline points="130,355 100,355 100,192" fill="none" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="370" y="270" font-size="17" fill="#1e3a8a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="end">4 to 20 mA</text>
<text x="370" y="292" font-size="17" fill="#1e3a8a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="end">loop current</text>
<text x="205" y="412" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Same 2 wires: power and signal</text>
<rect x="420" y="120" width="150" height="80" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="495.0" y="154.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Power supply</text>
<text x="495.0" y="177.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">AC or DC</text>
<rect x="630" y="120" width="140" height="80" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="700.0" y="154.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Transmitter</text>
<text x="700.0" y="177.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">field device</text>
<line x1="570" y1="140" x2="630" y2="140" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="3"/>
<line x1="570" y1="180" x2="630" y2="180" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="3"/>
<text x="600" y="218" font-size="17" fill="#dc2626" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">2 power</text>
<text x="600" y="238" font-size="17" fill="#dc2626" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">wires</text>
<rect x="610" y="320" width="160" height="70" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="690.0" y="349.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">PLC analog</text>
<text x="690.0" y="372.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">input</text>
<line x1="665" y1="200" x2="665" y2="320" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="3"/>
<line x1="715" y1="200" x2="715" y2="320" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="3"/>
<text x="655" y="270" font-size="17" fill="#1e3a8a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="end">2 signal</text>
<text x="655" y="292" font-size="17" fill="#1e3a8a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="end">wires</text>
<text x="595" y="412" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Power pair and signal pair kept apart</text>
<text x="400" y="470" font-size="17" fill="#4b5563" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">In the 2 wire loop the DC supply, transmitter and PLC input are in series,</text>
<text x="400" y="496" font-size="17" fill="#4b5563" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">while the 4 wire type has its own AC or DC power connection.</text>
</svg>

figs.name: 2-wire-and-4-wire-transmitter-selection-flowchart
figs.alt: flowchart for choosing a loop powered 2 wire transmitter or a 4 wire transmitter
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog showing when to use a 4 wire transmitter for high power or voltage output, and when a loop powered 2 wire transmitter can be used.
figs.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 540" width="100%" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif">
<title>Flowchart to choose a 2 wire or 4 wire transmitter</title>
<rect width="800" height="540" fill="#ffffff"/>
<defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0 0L10 5L0 10z" fill="#1a2b4a"/></marker></defs>
<text x="400.0" y="34" font-size="24" fill="#1e3a8a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Choosing 2 Wire or 4 Wire Wiring</text>
<rect x="90" y="55" width="340" height="56" rx="10" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="260.0" y="89.3" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Select transmitter wiring</text>
<line x1="260" y1="111" x2="260" y2="146" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<polygon points="260,148.0 430.0,200 260,252.0 90.0,200" fill="#fef3c7" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="260" y="195.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Needs high power</text>
<text x="260" y="216.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">or voltage output?</text>
<line x1="430" y1="200" x2="498" y2="200" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="462" y="190" font-size="17" fill="#1e3a8a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Yes</text>
<rect x="500" y="165" width="280" height="70" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="640.0" y="194.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">4 wire transmitter</text>
<text x="640.0" y="217.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">two power, two signal wires</text>
<line x1="260" y1="252" x2="260" y2="290" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="282" y="278" font-size="17" fill="#4b5563" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">No</text>
<polygon points="260,293.0 430.0,345 260,397.0 90.0,345" fill="#fef3c7" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="260" y="340.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Designed to be</text>
<text x="260" y="361.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">loop powered?</text>
<line x1="430" y1="345" x2="498" y2="345" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="462" y="335" font-size="17" fill="#1e3a8a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">No</text>
<rect x="500" y="310" width="280" height="70" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="640.0" y="339.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">4 wire transmitter</text>
<text x="640.0" y="362.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">separate AC or DC supply</text>
<line x1="260" y1="397" x2="260" y2="428" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="285" y="418" font-size="17" fill="#4b5563" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Yes</text>
<rect x="90" y="430" width="340" height="84" rx="10" fill="#dcfce7" stroke="#15803d" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="260.0" y="454.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">2 wire transmitter</text>
<text x="260.0" y="477.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">DC supply, transmitter and</text>
<text x="260.0" y="500.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">PLC input in series</text>
<line x1="430" y1="472" x2="498" y2="472" stroke="#15803d" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<rect x="500" y="430" width="280" height="84" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#15803d" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="640.0" y="454.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Why it is popular</text>
<text x="640.0" y="477.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">fewer cables, low power,</text>
<text x="640.0" y="500.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">simple installation</text>
</svg>

figs.name: 2-wire-and-4-wire-current-vs-voltage-signal-infographic
figs.alt: voltage signal drop on a long cable compared with a current loop that stays the same
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog showing why transmitters use current signals: a voltage signal drops along cable resistance, while current in a series loop is the same at every point.
figs.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 520" width="100%" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif">
<title>Why current signals are preferred over voltage signals on long transmitter cables</title>
<rect width="800" height="520" fill="#ffffff"/>
<defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0 0L10 5L0 10z" fill="#1a2b4a"/></marker></defs>
<text x="400.0" y="34" font-size="24" fill="#1e3a8a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Why Current Signals Beat Voltage on Long Cables</text>
<rect x="20" y="60" width="760" height="190" rx="14" fill="#fef2f2" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="40" y="90" font-size="20" fill="#b91c1c" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Voltage signal</text>
<rect x="45" y="110" width="150" height="70" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="120.0" y="139.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Transmitter</text>
<text x="120.0" y="162.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">sends voltage</text>
<rect x="600" y="110" width="160" height="70" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="680.0" y="139.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">PLC input</text>
<text x="680.0" y="162.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">reads less</text>
<polyline points="195,145 300,145 312,130 336,160 360,130 384,160 408,130 432,160 456,130 480,160 498,145 600,145" fill="none" stroke="#b91c1c" stroke-width="3"/>
<text x="400" y="196" font-size="17" fill="#b91c1c" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Long cable resistance</text>
<text x="400" y="232" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Voltage drop along the cable gives an inaccurate reading</text>
<rect x="20" y="265" width="760" height="235" rx="14" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="40" y="295" font-size="20" fill="#1e3a8a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Current signal, series loop</text>
<rect x="150" y="320" width="500" height="120" fill="none" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="3"/>
<rect x="65" y="345" width="150" height="70" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="140.0" y="374.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Transmitter</text>
<text x="140.0" y="397.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">sends mA</text>
<rect x="585" y="345" width="160" height="70" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="665.0" y="374.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">PLC input</text>
<text x="665.0" y="397.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">reads mA</text>
<circle cx="330" cy="320" r="27" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1e3a8a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<text x="330" y="326" font-size="17" fill="#1e3a8a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">mA</text>
<circle cx="470" cy="320" r="27" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1e3a8a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<text x="470" y="326" font-size="17" fill="#1e3a8a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">mA</text>
<circle cx="400" cy="440" r="27" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1e3a8a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<text x="400" y="446" font-size="17" fill="#1e3a8a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">mA</text>
<text x="400" y="385" font-size="17" fill="#1e3a8a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">All meters read the same</text>
<text x="400" y="488" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Current is the same at every point, so cable length does not change it</text>
</svg>
